messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: node gpu-rt-11 reported repeated OOMs and CUDA driver resets (5xx) — auto-suppress 60s
jen (sre): seeing container crash loops on node gpu-rt-11, kernel logs show 'CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS' + 'out of memory' around same time
matt (runtime): confirmed: paged-attention allocator growth on that host. kv-store fragment count increasing, free pages not being reclaimed. timeline matches slow creep over ~18 hours
luis (oncall): rolling mitigation ideas? can we drain the node safely without dropping in-flight requests?
jen (sre): start with scaling down concurrency on that node: set node annotation rwi/concurrency=1; also reduce default batch size for model serving group 'gpt-small-rt' to cut KV pressure
kate (pm): any customer-visible errors yet? support queue ticking up?
support-bot: Alert: 3 customer reports in last 30m complaining about 500s and failed generations. Affected tenants: acme-inc (prod), beta-app (staging), internal-loadtest
matt (runtime): logs (excerpt):
```
2026-03-15T03:12:22Z runtime: alloc_pages: allocated=124312 free_pages=130 pending_frag=412
2026-03-15T03:16:11Z runtime: kv_cache: fragment_count=412 -> 579, leak_est=167MB
2026-03-15T03:18:09Z cuda: driver_reset detected on gpu-2: reason=illegal_address
2026-03-15T03:18:15Z container: exit_code=137, oom_kill
```
matt (runtime): looks like fragmentation + slow leak triggered periodic OOMs; paging to device mem increases latency then fails
jen (sre): mitigation plan A (non-disruptive): enable aggressive eviction on KV cache for model pool 'gpt-small-rt' via /admin/config
jen (sre): command to apply (k8s config patch):
```
kubectl -n inference patch configmap runtime-config --type=json -p='[
  {"op":"add","path":"/kv_cache/eviction_threshold","value":"0.55"},
  {"op":"add","path":"/kv_cache/enable_fragment_defrag","value":"true"}
]'
```
matt (runtime): we have a flag to disable page-based allocator fallback: runtime.flags.paged_alloc=false — that'll force resident allocation (may reduce fragmentation) but increases immediate memory pressure; only do if freeing KV cache reduces footprint
luis (oncall): initiating drain of gpu-rt-11 now: kubectl cordon/drain. Will route traffic to standby pool. Expect ~90s of graceful shift
luis (oncall): cordon done. drain in progress. dropping concurrency on nodes still serving this pool to limit new inflight batches
kate (pm): ETA to full recovery? customers? we should notify Acme support lead (sarah@acme)
jen (sre): timeline: eviction patch + cache defrag should start reclaiming in ~2-5m. If OOMs persist, we will restart runtime pods on that node to flush allocator state
matt (runtime): performing a rolling restart of runtime pods on that node: kubectl rollout restart deployment/runtime-gpu-pool --field-selector spec.nodeName=gpu-rt-11
support-bot: Customer impact update: Acme-inc seeing 8 failed requests/min, beta-app intermittent timeouts, internal-loadtest spikes in p95 latency
jen (sre): after eviction enabled we saw fragment_count drop: 579 -> 210 in logs, reclaimed ~220MB
matt (runtime): good sign. however there are still sporadic driver resets on gpu-2. pushing a driver debug dump to /tmp/driver_dumps
luis (oncall): pods restarted. node stable for 4m, no new OOMs. marking incident as 'mitigated' but not resolved
kate (pm): raising an incident notes to customers: brief outage window 03:12–03:30 UTC; apologies. draft sent to comms for approval
matt (runtime): follow-up: need a root-cause ticket: probable bug in paged allocator interaction with KV cache eviction path causing stale page refs leading to fragment bleed. assigning to eng/runtime team
jen (sre): oncall handoff: I'm handing to luis; I'll remain on-call until handoff complete. luis, take over escalation if OOMs reappear
luis (oncall): taking over. current state: node drained, eviction enabled, restarted pods, driver resets reduced. monitoring p95 and failed_requests metrics
support-bot: metrics snapshot: failed_requests total=124 in window, p95 latency increased from 320ms -> 2.1s during peak
kate (pm): customers to patch: Acme-prod (high), Beta-app (med). We should offer warm-seat support and post-incident writeup
matt (runtime): short-term follow-ups: add a safety throttle for kv_cache growth; add clearer healthcheck for allocator fragmentation (fragment_count>400 trigger); bake defrag routine into regular GC
jen (sre): long-term: plan a runtime patch to fix stale refs + add automated rolling restarts for nodes hitting fragmentation threshold to avoid manual handoffs
luis (oncall): handing to next shift in 2h. Recorded mitigation steps in incident doc: /incidents/2412345678-kv-drift-node-flap-incident
kate (pm): assigning postmortem owners: matt (runtime), jen (sre). Support to craft customer communication
matt (runtime): note for postmortem: attach driver dumps, allocator traces, and config diff. Also include model traffic traces for the affected tenant (acme-inc)
jen (sre): closing note: if anyone sees regressions or repeated OOMs, ping @luis and escalate to infra-eng
luis (oncall): closing thread here — monitoring continues for next 1h. :white_check_mark:
